doc.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Past D.C. jazz documentaries with Billy Taylor
summary: Murphy recalls Wess and Billy Taylor recounting D.C. jazz history for NPR and the Kennedy Center; Wess rarely goes back to Washington.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: and I was working on a program for NPR, for their jazz profiles series. I was doing a history of jazz in Washington, D.C. You and Billy had a great conversation, remembering the details, and Billy remembered situation after situation. You were able to fill all the names of the players, all the obscure clubs that ever-existed anywhere in Washington.
That was then; I can’t remember anything! (Laughs)

Time has passed since 2000. I saw that you did it again in some measure, for a program that was at the Kennedy Center in 2008. It was about the history of jazz in D.C. Do you recall that? I had thought it was a live program that you and Billy did but he said that, again, you were maybe filmed at his apartment. Do you have any recollection of that?
I think we were walking around Washington a bit, I don’t know.
We saw some of the places of where they were, or something, as I remember. But anyways, I know what you’re talking about.
And how often do you get back to D.C.?
Well, not too often. I don’t have any reason to go there, really, unless Billy calls me for the summer. Other than that I don’t have any reason to go to Washington.
